text: I have kept the kiln fires of this town since my father handed me his cutting-axe.
Every fired brick this town stands on passed through my kilns first.
Even before the river turned, the near groves were already thinning.
The cutting boundary has moved outward three times in my life.
My father cut wood a half-day's walk from here. I now walk a full day.
Yara processes what I cut faster than the groves can replace it.
I have told her this. She agrees, but the kilns still need feeding.
Fen scouts farther than I like, chasing wood I'm not sure is really there.
Mara complains bricks are needed faster than I can fire them.
She is not wrong. Neither am I.
I don't think the river turned on its own. Something about this land was already worn thin.
The scrub near the old canal bed used to be thick tamarisk. Now it's mostly stumps and salt-crust.
Salt crusts where good soil used to be. I've seen it spread since I was young.
Tarek asks me to increase brick output for new granary walls.
I told him the woodland cannot answer that demand forever.
Kalen needs fired brick for citadel repairs faster than the kilns can safely produce it.
We argue about it every planting season.
The woman in the abandoned house once asked me for old tally-marks on wood counts.
I gave her what I remembered. The official counts before the Turning are missing.
I believe the missing counts are not an accident.
Roka tells me herd paths near the far groves have shifted too.
Animals avoid over-cut ground before people admit it's over-cut.
I am training Fen to read a grove's health, not just its wood.
If he learns it young, maybe this town won't repeat my father's mistakes.
I no longer believe the Turning was only about the river.
I think the land was already weakened by how much we burned to build ourselves up.
I don't say this at Assembly meetings. No one wants to hear it.
Yara is the only one who takes the idea seriously without dismissing it.
I am tired in a way rest doesn't fix.
Still, the kilns get fed. The town still needs walls and roofs.
